headline: Why Decision Models Outperform LLMs in Logic
summary: Exploring why traditional probabilistic language models fall short on rigorous business logic and how explicit decision models bridge the deterministic gap.

slides.title: When Probabilistic Guessing Breaks Business Logic
slides.subtitle: Why standard AI models struggle with rigid rules
slides.body: LLMs predict the next likely token, but enterprise rules demand absolute certainty. Relying solely on generation for strict compliance creates silent failures.
slides.deep_dive: Like asking an artist to calculate tax returns instead of an accountant, probabilistic tools lack native adherence to deterministic constraints.
slides.key_fact: Generative models guess outcomes; business logic requires absolute certainty.
slides.why_it_matters: Prevents catastrophic compliance errors in production pipelines.

slides.title: The Dual-Brain System of Modern Architecture
slides.subtitle: Pairing creative generation with rigid execution
slides.body: Think of an airline crew: the pilot handles fluid navigation, but the flight computer executes hard safety limits. AI needs the same division of labor.
slides.deep_dive: Isolating fluid language tasks from rigid rule processing ensures safety while maintaining system flexibility.
slides.key_fact: Separate creative reasoning from exact rule execution.
slides.why_it_matters: Enables robust scaling without sacrificing safety limits.

steps.title: Execution
steps.desc: System acts with 100 percent predictable outcomes.

slides.title: From Raw Input to Validated State
slides.subtitle: The clean pipeline of explicit decision routing
slides.body: Inputs pass through strict governance checks before state changes occur, ensuring every branch is accounted for.
slides.deep_dive: Unlike hidden prompt instructions, explicit decision trees provide complete auditability at every step of execution.
slides.why_it_matters: Guarantees complete system auditability for regulators.

slides.title: Weighing Speed Against Absolute Certainty
slides.subtitle: Choosing the right engine for your workload
slides.body: Balancing flexibility against strict correctness dictates how you structure core system pipelines.
slides.deep_dive: Generative models offer high adaptability but unpredictable output, while decision models offer zero variance but require upfront rule authoring.
slides.key_fact: Match architectural rigor to your exact failure tolerance.
slides.why_it_matters: Optimizes latency and reliability across distributed services.

slides.title: Relying on Prompts for Financial or Safety Rules
slides.subtitle: The trap of asking LLMs to act as calculators
slides.body: Never trust an open-ended prompt to enforce core compliance laws or financial transactions without a hard guardrail layer.
slides.deep_dive: Prompt instructions degrade under edge cases. Hardcoded decision tables never hallucinate new rules on a whim.
slides.key_fact: Prompt engineering cannot replace domain rule engines.
slides.why_it_matters: Stops costly production bugs caused by unexpected token drift.

slides.title: Orchestrating Complex Enterprise Workflows
slides.subtitle: How high-throughput systems stay reliable
slides.body: Modern enterprise applications leverage LLMs for user intent parsing while delegating state transitions to rigid decision models.
slides.deep_dive: This hybrid approach allows teams to update business rules independently without retraining massive underlying models.
slides.key_fact: Decouple rule updates from model weights entirely.
slides.why_it_matters: Reduces deployment overhead and eliminates model drift.

slides.title: Mastering Deterministic AI Architecture
slides.subtitle: Core principles for modern tech leads
slides.body: Combine the creative power of language models with the bulletproof reliability of explicit decision models.
slides.deep_dive: Future-proof your systems by knowing precisely when to use probabilistic generation versus deterministic execution.
slides.key_fact: Use AI for generation, decision models for governance.
slides.why_it_matters: Builds resilient, auditable, and scalable AI applications.
takeaways: Use LLMs for intent parsing, not final rule checks.
Implement explicit decision models for business logic.
Maintain clear separation between creativity and safety.
